title: Barely strips herbs and barely cuts
text:
Barely strips herbs and barely cuts. I had high expectations for these shears but was sorely disappointed and here is why:

- The shears don't cut well at all unless I put the herb stem all the way to the base of the shear (that's the intersection of the cutting blades) . The tip has minimal cutting power unless the item being cut is delicate -- like cutting chives.

- The handle lock requires force to close.

- The herb stripper slot is awkward to use, especially for items with bigger leaves that have to be "fed through the handle" in order to reach the slot. Although I was partially successful in removing thyme from its branch that only worked when the branch wasn't delicate enough to break on its own.

The only thing I like about these shears is that the rubberized handle feels good in my hand and provides me with a non-slip grip when the shears are open.

I cannot recommend these and would purchase kitchen shears instead. This is another item that will eventually head to the landfill. I will continue to use my thumb and forefinger to strip herbs as I always do and will use my standard kitchen shears to do all the cutting work.
